Open when a task reads a term row or the id rules. The starting point is `docs/guides/law-using-the-official-corpus.md`.
## Terminology glossary (EN↔CN)
The corpus's bilingual EN ↔ CN term map — controls, nodes, events, parameters and unit statuses keyed by
`path_id`, with the terms that have no clean counterpart flagged rather than invented. It records one confirmed
locale defect in the source (§ 9.1: the Lua 5.3 stdlib blacklist differs between the two language editions) and
settles the caps-table difference reported in the task brief (§ 9.2). **`§ 11` supersedes § 8 (a)'s eleven `no clean counterpart`
verdicts, using the `cn`-region feed's own CN titles — read § 11 before treating any § 8 (a) row as a term the
Chinese corpus lacks; § 8 stands as the dated pass that wrote it.** Corpus counts are stated only in this file's
§ *Counts*; the glossary carries none.
### Preamble — not an imported article
This glossary carries no `path_id`, no `real_id`, no `section`, no `tier` and no `source_url`, because it mirrors
nothing: it is this repo's cross-language term map *over* the corpus, and the front-matter field set of
`docs/specs/ugc-corpus-home-and-layout.md` § 4 is an article's, not a glossary's. `corpus:` still
says which corpus the file belongs to, so a file pasted out of it says whose it is; `lang:` is the honest bilingual marker
`en-cn`, which is deliberately **not** one of the feed's two locale codes (`en-us`, `zh-cn`) and is therefore not a
directory name anywhere. `method:` keeps § 4's token vocabulary (`transcription`), with the note saying what was
transcribed. From 2026-09-27 this glossary is folded into the corpus's root document,
`docs/guides/law-using-the-official-corpus.md`
(the former `00-glossary.md`, which sat beside the former `00-index.md` at the corpus root).
**Which language is which, once.** **CN is what a CN client session shows** — the strings a player and the
千星沙箱 editor render on the `zh-cn` portal, and the only wording that matches the shipped UI. **EN is what this
repo's docs use** — the `en-us` portal's wording, which `AGENTS.md` § *Localization* and `CONTEXT.md` are written
in. A row's two cells are therefore not "one term, two spellings of it": they are the two source languages' own
terms, and a mismatch between them is a fact about the platform, not about this repo's copy (§ 8, § 9).
### 1. Which id is which, in one paragraph
`path_id` is the cross-language key and the URL segment: it is what filenames are keyed on, and the only thing
that lets a row point at both trees at once. `real_id` is the **language-local** feed key — the key into
`headingsMap.json` / `textMap.json` — and the two id sets share no value across languages, so a tree keyed on
`real_id` cannot find its own counterpart. **In `zh-cn`, `path_id === real_id` for every node**; in `en-us` they
differ. That equality is the trap: a CN-side check that "joins" on a `real_id` silently passes, and a
worker who confuses the two on the CN tree reports a join that the EN tree contradicts — this work wave gave one

Topic: platform, layout
## Law
The two decisions that were written conditioned on the phase gate — the platform-free core carve-out (`ADR-0002`) and
the art-loads-in-source / code-owned-sprites pair (`ADR-0004`, `ADR-0005`) — stand **on their own ground**. Their

surface and per shared concern, run under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload
dependency; art is loaded into the map as editor image assets and never drawn at runtime; gameplay sprites enter code
as data and render through client controls. The nine platform questions stay open as **questions** in
`docs/specs/platform-facts.md` — measurements nobody has taken — and nothing reserves their answering to a human or
forbids an agent to record a measured answer; an answer lands where it is measured.

enforced by the static gate module named in that record — that gate is a linter, unrelated to the retired rule, and

- **`ADR-0004` — the art ruling stands; the closure clause is cut.** "in-editor checks no agent may close" is
withdrawn; the checks are open measurements, not a reserved closure.
- **`ADR-0005` — the code-owned-sprites ruling stands; its duration clause is cut.** "Source code remains outside this
change while the phase gate is open" is withdrawn.
- **No rule is weakened and none is strengthened.** This record removes a condition; it changes no decision's
substance. Where a conditioned record said "X, while the gate is open", it now says "X".

The durable-rule shelf `docs/specs/` lives in the template checkout, which is outside this repository, at the same two absolute roots as the measurement table under Stack, and this repo has none. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. A `build/` or `scratchpad/` folder is disposable wherever it sits and is never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5. Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-014-open-local-lua-54-runs-forbidden-constructs.md`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, which is outside this repository: `C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `AAAAA` device, `C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `TZ` device. This repo's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` is only a pointer to it. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.
<!-- device-path: C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template ; C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template -->

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7. Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. One exception: measured platform rows live in the template checkout, not in this repo, which is why Stack names them by absolute path. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block, as Stack's does. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>

diffs.oldText:
### Platform

- **Miliastra Wonderland** (千星奇域): Genshin's official UGC platform — players enter published maps, creators author them. Avoid: Genshin UGC mode, the Roblox thing.
- **Miliastra Sandbox** (千星沙箱): the PC-only authoring editor; it holds the platform's two places to write game logic — the node graph (the half that runs on the server) and client controls with Lua client scripts. Avoid: the editor, the sandbox (unqualified), "the scripting language" for the client half.
- **Client control**: a 2D UI element authored in the Sandbox and driven at runtime by a Lua client script — image, text, deck selector, UI effect, container. A control renders code-owned gameplay sprite data. Avoid: UI element, widget, node, sprite (the art data shown, never the control showing it).
- **Platform-free core** (可移植核心): the pure-Lua rules region in `platform-free-core/` — it names no client control, no save variable and no platform call. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. Avoid: engine, framework, backend, library.
- **Cloud-save variable**: the platform's only persistence — no filesystem, no OS save file (`PRD.md` § 5.1). Avoid: save file, state.json, local storage.
- **Sprite** (精灵图): code-owned gameplay art data rendered through a client control, never an externally uploaded or imported gameplay image (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay. Avoid: asset pipeline, texture, atlas, resource, drawable.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, named under Stack below; do not copy a row here. A rule that is still true about how to work is a `law-` file under `docs/guides/`; a product or content rule is an ADR under `docs/adr/`. The durable-rule shelf `docs/specs/` is the template's, at that checkout's `docs/specs/` (checkout roots under Stack); this repo has none. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. A `build/` or `scratchpad/` folder is disposable wherever it sits and is never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5. Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

{"content":"# ADR index

One line per decision. **Hand-maintained** — there is no generator, so adding an ADR means adding its
row here. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`.

The next number is derived by listing `docs/adr/`, never from this line.

Row grammar: the `Law` cell **mirrors that record's in-force `Law:` line verbatim** — never a summary,
no *Consequences* prose, no re-bolded clause (`docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` § *File anatomy*).
A changed rule is edited in place in its record, so the cell always states what that ADR is now; where
a record carries a `Superseded-by`/`Supersedes` line, the cell adds that one plain cross-reference —
no dated qualifier, no amendment note.

| ID | Topic | Law |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ADR-0001](ADR-0001-product-names.md) | naming | The product is named EN *Taskworld Project*, CN **Sandbox-City**; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo and code name, internal and never player-facing. |
| [ADR-0002](ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md) | platform, layout | The platform-free core is Lua naming no platform call, control, save-variable runtime form, coordinate or cap; it may be organised per surface and per shared concern, runs only under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload dependency, and its 5.1-safe subset is enforced by a static gate module rather than by that runtime — whose 5.4.5 accepts every banned construct. *(superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate conditioning clause only)* |
| [ADR-0003](ADR-0003-carry-over-ratification.md) | rules, content | The source game's rules, content and data tables carry over as design seed and nothing else does — no line of code, no file of audio, font or string, and not the previous attempt's genshin-ts toolchain — with the seed corpus's `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B* named as the conflict authority for its content figures. |
| [ADR-0004](ADR-0004-art-loads-in-source-undecided.md) | art | Art is loaded into the map as editor image assets and never drawn at runtime, so it costs a budget rather than code; the salvaged example's runtime rect-explosion shape is rejected as the shipping shape, and which art source the project uses stays an open human decision. *(superseded for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering by ADR-0005; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate closure clause)* |
| [ADR-0005](ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md) | art, platform | Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls with no external gameplay image upload/import path; cover imagery is outside gameplay, and the data/control budget remains an open A5/A9 human gate. *(supersedes ADR-0004 for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate duration clause)* |
| [ADR-0006](ADR-0006-retire-the-phase-gate-condition.md) | platform, layout | The two decisions conditioned on the phase gate (`ADR-0002` core carve-out, `ADR-0004`/`ADR-0005` art and sprite rulings) stand on their own ground; their gate-conditioning clauses are withdrawn and no rule is weakened. The nine platform questions stay open as questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md` § Open questions, unanswerable by no agent and reserved to no human. |

AGENTS.md:19: Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5. Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.
AGENTS.md:33: - Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7. Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.
CONTEXT.md:13: - **Cloud-save variable**: the platform's only persistence — no filesystem, no OS save file (`PRD.md` § 5.1). Avoid: save file, state.json, local storage.
PRD.md:11: The stack, editor constraints and platform caveats live in `AGENTS.md` § Stack; this document designs inside 5.1's constraints and waits on 5.2's assumptions.
PRD.md:55: | Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md` § Stack). |
PRD.md:64: What the device has actually measured — layout, the tick, per-control text, runtime control creation, the caps and the sprite budget — lives in the template checkout, outside this repo: `C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `AAAAA` device, `C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `TZ` device. This repo keeps no measured row: `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` is a pointer to that file. What remains unknown — cross-session save, group show/hide, cloud-save scope — is kept as open questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md` § Open questions. Design against the measured rows in the template's table; the open questions have one `Type: research` issue each, and each resolves into an ADR where the answer changes architecture. The earlier practice of treating these as assumptions to be gated is retired (see `AGENTS.md` § Stack).
PRD.md:69: The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md` § Verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.
PRD.md:214: | R2 | ~~Layout rule. While any of A1-A9 is open this project holds no source layout: no module tree, scene tree, asset tree or control inventory is scaffolded on a guess.~~ **Withdrawn 2026-10-02:** the phase-gate layout law this row expressed is void — agent-authored template boilerplate with no human ratification. The layout question now lives in `AGENTS.md` § Stack, and in the open questions at `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md` § Open questions; `ADR-0006` records the retirement. The number is kept, not reused. |

diffs.oldText:
- **Miliastra Sandbox** (千星沙箱): the PC-only authoring editor; it holds the platform's two places to write game logic — the node graph (the half that runs on the server) and client controls with Lua client scripts. Avoid: the editor, the sandbox (unqualified), "the scripting language" for the client half.
- **Client control**: a 2D UI element authored in the Sandbox and driven at runtime by a Lua client script — image, text, deck selector, UI effect, container. A control renders code-owned gameplay sprite data. Avoid: UI element, widget, node, sprite (the art data shown, never the control showing it).
- **Platform-free core** (可移植核心): the pure-Lua rules region in `platform-free-core/` — it names no client control, no save variable and no platform call. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. Avoid: engine, framework, backend, library.
- **Cloud-save variable**: the platform's only persistence — no filesystem, no OS save file (`PRD.md` § 5.1). Avoid: save file, state.json, local storage.
- **Sprite** (精灵图): code-owned gameplay art data rendered through a client control, never an externally uploaded or imported gameplay image (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay. Avoid: asset pipeline, texture, atlas, resource, drawable.

### Scope

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, named under Stack below; do not copy a row here. A rule that is still true about how to work is a `law-` file under `docs/guides/`; a product or content rule is an ADR under `docs/adr/`. The durable-rule shelf `docs/specs/` is the template's, inside that same checkout and not this repository. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. A `build/` or `scratchpad/` folder is disposable wherever it sits and is never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5. Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-014-open-local-lua-54-runs-forbidden-constructs.md`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, which is outside this repository: `C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `AAAAA` device, `C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `TZ` device. This repo's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` is only a pointer to it. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.
<!-- device-path: C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template ; C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template -->

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7. Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. One exception: measured platform rows live in the template checkout, not in this repo, which is why Stack names them by absolute path. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block, as Stack's does. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

{"content":"# 00-log — template resync, 2026-10-24

Scope: the 74 Markdown files listed in the task — `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `PRD.md`, every `.md`
under `docs/project/`, `docs/guides/` and `docs/adr/`. Nothing outside that set was edited.

One row per thing changed or deliberately left alone. Status is `changed` or `left alone, because …`.
Every file edited in this pass appears as at least one row.

## Deliverable 1 — the seven indexes match their directories

| # | What was wrong | Why it mattered | Files changed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `docs/project/index.md` listed paths that do not exist in this repo: `building/index.md`, `platform/index.md`, `sessions/index.md` (no `docs/project/` prefix), and a `../miliastra-game-template/...` measurement table. `ref-glossary.md` and `ref-official-docs.md` were named without their folder, and `docs/specs/` was routed to as a live shelf. | A reader following the routing table landed on nothing, and the index did not describe its own directory. | `docs/project/index.md` | changed |
| 2 | `docs/project/building/index.md` listed 14 entries for 13 files, naming `phase0-protocols/index.md` as if it were a sibling `.md` file rather than a folder index. | The building shelf's own index disagreed with the disk by one entry. | left alone, because the comparison found all 13 files listed and the fourteenth token is the folder's own index, which the line correctly describes; the count is 13 files plus one sub-index, and every file in the folder is listed. | left alone, because the entry set is correct |
| 3 | `docs/project/platform/index.md` already listed both files in its folder. | No defect. | none | left alone, because the index already matched its directory |
| 4 | `docs/project/sessions/index.md` cited `ref-shaping-laws.md` as if it sat in this folder; that file is the template's. | The index named a file absent from the directory and from the repo. | `docs/project/sessions/index.md` | changed |
| 5 | `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/index.md` already listed all 20 files in its folder. | No defect. | none | left alone, because the index already matched its directory |
| 6 | `docs/adr/index.md` had one row per ADR in its Law table but no filename column, so the six record files were not listed as files, and it named `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md` and the seed corpus's `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` with no resolvable path. | The ADR index is the live list of decisions, and a reader could not get from a row to its record. | `docs/adr/index.md` | changed |
| 7 | `docs/guides/index.md` already listed all 19 files in its folder. | No defect. | none | left alone, because the index already matched its directory |

## Deliverable 2 — every repo-relative path in the five entry documents resolves

| # | What was wrong | Why it mattered | Files changed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | `AGENTS.md` § Stack and § Editing cited `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` as a repo-relative sibling path. No such sibling exists from this checkout. | The one path every measurement rule depends on led nowhere. | `AGENTS.md` | changed — the template is now named as an external checkout, with both device roots and a `<!-- device-path: -->` marker |
| 9 | `AGENTS.md` named `docs/specs/` as a shelf of this repo, and `build/` and `scratchpad/` as disposable folders, none of which exist here. | The paragraph told a reader to use shelves this repo does not have. | `AGENTS.md` | changed — `docs/specs/` is now the template's shelf, and `build/`/`scratchpad/` are described as disposable wherever they sit |
| 10 | `PRD.md` § 5.1 and § 5.2 cited the template's measurement table as a sibling path, and § 5.2 told the reader to design against rows "in ENGINE.md", a file that does not exist in this repo or the template. | The platform-facts section pointed at a missing file and a missing sibling. | `PRD.md` | changed — the template checkout and both device roots are named, and the ENGINE.md reference is now the template's measurement table |
| 11 | `PRD.md` cited bare seed-corpus filenames (`DESIGN_UGC_*.md`, `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md`) with no folder, so none resolved. | Those are the source of every content figure in § 7; a reader could not open one. | `PRD.md` | changed — each cite now carries its full repo-relative path under `docs/plans/2026-05-27-previous-attempt-design-corpus/` |
| 12 | `PRD.md` D2 referred to a pixel pack "once held under `assets/`", a path that does not exist now and cannot be opened. | It read as a live path. | `PRD.md` | changed — it now says the folder was a repo-root one and was removed by human ruling |
| 13 | `CONTEXT.md` cited the template's measurement table as `../miliastra-game-template/...`, and its index row gave that same non-resolving sibling path. | The glossary is the path index; a bad row there propagates. | `CONTEXT.md` | changed — the template checkout and both device roots are named once, with a `device-path` marker |
| 14 | `docs/project/index.md` and `docs/guides/index.md` — see rows 1, 6, 24 and 25. | Same class of defect. | `docs/project/index.md`, `docs/adr/index.md`, `docs/project/sessions/index.md` | changed |
| 15 | `AGENTS.md` cited the dialect probe as a bare `ISSUE-014`. | A bare number does not resolve to a file. | `AGENTS.md` | changed — it now names `issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-014-open-local-lua-54-runs-forbidden-constructs.md` |

## Deliverable 3 — every "<file> § <heading>" names a real heading

| # | What was wrong | Why it mattered | Files changed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | `AGENTS.md` wrote `PRD.md` § Platform constraints; `PRD.md`'s heading is `## 5. Platform constraints`. | The section reference did not name the heading. | `AGENTS.md` | changed to § 5. Platform constraints |
| 17 | `AGENTS.md` wrote `PRD.md` § Content of record; the heading is `## 7. Content of record`. | Same defect. | `AGENTS.md` | changed to § 7. Content of record |
| 18 | `AGENTS.md` relied on headings `Stack and platform`, `Platform facts and open questions`, `Visual verification` — none exists in `AGENTS.md`. | Three section citations pointed at headings that were renamed or never existed. | `AGENTS.md` (and the `PRD.md` lines that cite them) | changed — the citations now name `§ Stack` and `§ Verification`, which exist |
| 19 | `PRD.md` § 2 cited `AGENTS.md` (Stack and platform); § 5.1 cited `AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform; § 6.1 cited `AGENTS.md`, Visual verification; § 5.2 cited `AGENTS.md`, Platform facts and open questions; R2 cited `AGENTS.md` § *Platform facts and open questions*. | Four citations named headings absent from `AGENTS.md`. | `PRD.md` | changed — each now names a heading that exists (`§ Stack`, `§ Verification`, or the platform facts document) |
| 20 | `PRD.md` R2 said the layout question "lives in `AGENTS.md` § *Platform facts and open questions*". That heading does not exist there; the live home is `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`. | The withdrawn rule pointed at its own replacement by a heading that is not in the named file. | `PRD.md` | changed — it now cites `AGENTS.md` § Stack and the open-questions section of `ref-platform-facts.md` |
| 21 | `CONTEXT.md` cited `PRD.md` § 5.1 bare, with no heading text. | A numeric-only section reference does not name a heading. | `CONTEXT.md` | changed to § 5.1 What the build must live inside |
| 22 | `docs/guides/index.md` said `ref-official-terms-cn-halves.md` was "an appended amendment to § 11". The file is headed `11. Amendment to § 8 (a)`, so the index named the wrong section number. | A reader looking for § 11 in that file found the amendment's own number. | `docs/guides/index.md` | changed — it now quotes the file's real heading |
| 23 | Every other `<file> § <heading>` in the five entry documents was checked against its target file and resolves. | No defect found. | none | left alone, because every remaining reference names a heading that exists |

## Deliverable 4 — the template's conventions versus this repo's, decided

| # | What was wrong | Why it mattered | Files changed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24 | The template's `docs/project/index.md` has moved on: it keeps its own measurement rows (this repo points at them), it routes durable rules to a `docs/specs/` shelf that does not exist here, it caps a "chunk" at 250 lines where this repo caps a document at 150, it ends in-flight work by "written up or archived", and its `ref-glossary.md` holds the terms rather than pointing at `CONTEXT.md`. | Two live conventions documents disagreed, and the repo's own index neither said so nor decided. | `docs/project/index.md` | changed — a new subsection, "Conventions decided against the template, 2026-10-24", decides each difference in a table: keep the measurement pointer, keep no specs shelf, keep the 150-line cap, split by topic, keep settle-into-permanent-home, keep `CONTEXT.md` as the term authority |
| 25 | The same index's Routing table sent a measured fact and a durable rule to homes that only exist in the template, and named `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` without saying where plans live. | The routing table contradicted the conventions subsection added beside it. | `docs/project/index.md` | changed — the table now names the template for the measurement table, `docs/guides/` for working rules, `docs/adr/` for product rules, and `docs/plans/` for in-flight work |

## Deliverable 5 — this log

| # | What was wrong | Why it mattered | Files changed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26 | No record existed of what this resync changed or refused to change. | The pass would have been invisible to the next reader. | `docs/plans/2026-10-24-template-resync/00-log.md` | changed — this file |

## Things seen and deliberately left alone

| # | What was seen | Files | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 27 | Many files outside the five entry documents cite other repos (`../Genshin-IPC/...`), `docs/specs/...`, `build/...` and other paths that do not resolve here. | `docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-0006-retire-the-phase-gate-condition.md`, `docs/guides/law-doing-design-work.md`, `docs/project/building/ref-locale-bundles.md`, `docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`, `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/*.md`, `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`, `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-forensics.md` | left alone, because deliverable 2 and 3 are bounded to the five entry documents; these are outside that bound and repairing them would expand the scope |
| 28 | `docs/adr/ADR-0006-retire-the-phase-gate-condition.md` says the measured facts live in `docs/specs/platform-facts.md`, a path that does not exist in this repo or the template. | same file | left alone, because rewriting an ADR's body is a product decision for its owner, not a documentation resync edit |

## 1. Product statement

The player defends one open field: they place a handful of structures with their own hand, watch a timed enemy wave come at them, spend the Mora those kills returned on the next structure or the next upgrade, and finish the stage against a boss — in one sitting, on PC, alone. It is a 千星奇域 (Miliastra Wonderland) map driven by Lua client scripts and editor-authored client controls; its code name is `Taskworld-Project` (internal, never player-facing). The content set of record is the reduced set of section 7: 8 structures, 18 enemies, 5 stages, 12 enhancements, 6 talents, 8 items, 7 achievements.
## 2. Platform
The stack, editor constraints and platform caveats live in `AGENTS.md` (Stack and platform); this document designs inside 5.1's constraints and waits on 5.2's assumptions.
## 3. Goals and non-goals
### 3.1 Goals
A goal is what a good session looks like; each is checkable by playing, and each is measured by the rows named beside it.
| # | Goal | Measured by |
| G1 | A stranger clears Stage 1 on their first attempt and understands why if they lose. | F5, F12, F23, F29 |
| G2 | Every Mora movement is visible as a fact the moment it happens — the player can always say what they can afford. | F13-F21, NFR6, NFR7 |
| G3 | The build decision differs per stage: the roster, capacity and unlock chain force a different field each time. | F4-F11, F34 |
| G4 | A boss stage reads as a distinct fight — the phase flip is legible and winnable with prep, not with twitch. | F28, F9, F31 |
| G5 | Progress outlives the session: stages, stars, talents and achievements read back on the next visit, or degrade honestly. | F35-F39, NFR16 |
### 3.2 Non-goals
Named so nobody helpfully adds them later; each is out of scope for v1 with its reason.
- No multiplayer, no co-op, no shared stake: no server authority exists to arbitrate one, and the stake of a run is the player's own (R3, D3).
- No premium currency, no gacha, no purchase path, no payout of any kind (pillar 3, N1, N2).

- No tile grid, no maze-building constraint, no terrain cost: the field is continuous and open (`other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/02_MAP_AND_BUILDING.md`); a grid would be a different game.
- No external gameplay image upload/import path and no text-canvas composition; gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (N5, D2).

- No ported Flash code, no genshin-ts/TypeScript pipeline, no node-graph logic for v1 mechanics: the code examples in the seed corpus (the previous attempt's design documents) are read with that caveat; logic is re-typed as Lua client scripts.
- No endless mode, no difficulty tiers beyond the recorded Normal pacing, no stage 6: out of scope, and only a human decision adds them.
- No persistence of in-stage state — balance, placed structures, wave index: a stage is a transaction (F39).
- No audio, fonts or 3D model content in v1 (N4, D1): the game must be fully playable silent (NFR13, NFR14).
- No mobile authoring or mobile acceptance target: the editor is PC-only (5.1); play on mobile is a look.
## 4. Product pillars
The small set of promises every design decision is checked against.
1. Readable command — the field reads as facts, not as motion. If a player cannot tell phase, balance, wave and threat apart at a glance, the surface is re-scoped, not animated harder.
2. One economy, one owner — the Mora (摩拉) ledger is one number changed by named events at one seam (F13); no display path, timer or animation may mint or burn it (NFR6, NFR10).

3. Economy posture — no real-money or platform-currency path anywhere: cosmetic-only stakes, no purchase path, no payout of any kind. Weaken it only by a human decision recorded in its own N row and, if it changes architecture, its own ADR.
## 5. Platform constraints
### 5.1 What the build must live inside
| Constraint | Consequence for this product |

| Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform). |

| Client-local and server-side are separate domains. | Single-player logic may sit client-local; anything whose outcome must match for all players lives in a server-side graph. Nothing shared-stake is designed before the multiplayer decision (R3, D3). |

| The simultaneous-visible-control budget is the binding constraint. | All surfaces share one visible-control budget; hiding a whole group is the only relief valve, and whether a script may do it is A7. If it may not, the split-map fallback (section 8.3) is the plan, not an emergency. |

| Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls. | No external gameplay image upload/import path exists. The measured sprite-data and control capacity lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; design against it. Cover imagery is outside gameplay. |

| Persistence is cloud-save variables only. No filesystem, no file I/O; whether `require` spans files is unresolved. | Persistent state is a variable with a capacity budget; a key registry with version stamps is needed before the first key is written (NFR16); save scope is A8. |

| Caps are documented, unit-less and scope-unconfirmed; the editor is PC-only. | Every printed cap digit is documentation, never a designable number — each is an early verification task (5.2), and layouts are designed against confirmed answers only. Playtesting on mobile is a look, not an edit. |

What the device has actually measured — layout, the tick, per-control text, runtime control creation, the caps and the sprite budget — lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, and what remains unknown — cross-session save, group show/hide, cloud-save scope — is kept as open questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`. Design against the measured rows in ENGINE.md; the open questions have one `Type: research` issue each, and each resolves into an ADR where the answer changes architecture. ## 6. Functional requirements

The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md`, Visual verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.

ID conventions: bare, dot-free identifiers, each in one registry — F functional requirement (6.1); G goal (3.1); N product posture row (6.5); NFR non-functional requirement (6.4); R standing rule (6.6); A platform assumption (5.2); D open product decision (6.7); S surface (6.2); M wiring piece (6.3). IDs are never reused for a different meaning.

## 8. Phasing, exit criteria and the split-map fallback
### 8.1 Phasing

- Phase 0 — a short investigation. It settles the open questions and builds almost nothing. Measure the open platform questions in writing (one research issue each), run the test procedures in `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/`, record every measured figure together with the work pass that measured it, and choose one of two routes: a single map, or the split-map fallback. Close the open decisions (D1, D2, D7) to the extent a human will; the platform-free core (the economy code, the tables, the wave scheduler and the random-number generator) is organised and exercised during Phase 0.

- Phase 1 — build the surfaces in parallel. One surface per owner, no two owners touching the same files, and nothing published in this phase — a half-built hub is not a map. Order does not matter; the wiring (M1-M7) is integrated last, and the integration owner is responsible for those wiring rows.
- Phase 2 — integrate, and publish once. Publication is one event, allowed only when the whole set passes (8.2); the publishing checklist is handed to the human, who alone publishes.
### 8.2 Whole-set exit criteria
The set a human reads before consenting to publication. Every row is pass/fail by playing; no row may be marked passed on the strength of an agent's own mockup.
1. Every 6.2 surface row passes its acceptance check and its NFR12 gate on the real map, in both locales.
2. Every 6.3 wiring row passes: one ledger (M2), one phase owner (M1), one persisted key registry (M4).
3. Every F-row's acceptance has been walked by a person who did not write it, in order, S1 to S6.
4. NFR1-NFR18 hold, or name their exception in writing; NFR12's gate has a dated human verdict beside it.

5. The platform questions of 5.2 are measured, each resolving into an ADR where the answer changes architecture — an unanswered question that a row depends on is a blocked publication, not a risk note.
6. Both locale key sets are identical, verified by opening both files, and the count is stamped at its home (`docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`).
7. D1, D2 and D7 are decided; where D2 is still open, no final gameplay sprite-data set claim may be made and the set fails.
8. A playtest path exists for all five stages end to end, silent and motion-off (NFR13, NFR14).
9. No row in this file cites an unconfirmed platform figure as its basis (R1, NFR17).
10. The creator-facing policy reading has happened by a human, and its name, version and date are recorded.
### 8.3 The split-map fallback — designed for from the start

If A7 answers that a script may not show and hide whole control groups, or if A5's confirmed count cannot hold S1-S6 at once, each surface becomes its own map with S1 as the entry point. Planned from the start, not used as a last resort:

- The economy stays in-run either way: Mora is session-scoped (F21), so the split never splits the balance; what the split threatens is read-back, and A8 decides whether one persisted key set survives across maps. If A8 answers per map, the progression data families (F36) must be given a new place or the campaign restructured — a scope change decided by a human, never absorbed silently.

- Cost named in advance: the phase driver (M1), ledger seam (M2) and the locale lookup (M7) are duplicated per map, and every hand-off between maps becomes an authored entry point rather than a show/hide.
- The exit criterion that changes: 8.2 row 1 is then checked per map, and row 5's A5/A7/A8 answers are the evidence attached to the decision.

lines.text: # ADR-0002 — the platform-free core, its carve-out, and who actually enforces the Lua subset
Status: **Accepted** (2026-09-28 — the overnight meta wave's instantiation instruction filling `AGENTS.md`
§ *Stack & platform*'s open slots; every figure below measured on disk and at the keyboard at `7e52c97`)
Topic: platform, layout

Law: The platform-free core is Lua naming no platform call, control, save-variable runtime form, coordinate or cap; it may be organised per surface and per shared concern, runs only under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload dependency, and its 5.1-safe subset is enforced by a static gate module rather than by that runtime — whose 5.4.5 accepts every banned construct.

Superseded-by: `ADR-0006` (2026-10-02) — **in part:** the *Context* statement "§ *Phase gate* withholds … layout" is withdrawn (the gate it named is void); the carve-out and the static gate module stand unweakened.
## Context
`AGENTS.md` § *Stack & platform* permits one command surface "except the platform-free core named by this
project's own ADRs (`<platform-free-core ADR id>`)", at `AGENTS.md:73` and again at `AGENTS.md:133`, and the
carve-out paragraph of `platform-free-core/README.md` § *The carve-out law* held the matching
`<carve-out ADR id>` slot — that slot is filled by this filing, and `CONTEXT.md:36-42` names the region by two
ids still waiting on the integrator. Disk before this
record held one ADR (`docs/adr/`), so the carve-out had no owner and the directory was, by its own pre-filing
§ *The carve-out law*, "the style exhibit only".
**The local runtime cannot police the subset.** Measured at the keyboard 2026-09-28: the interpreter on `PATH`
reports `Lua 5.4.5` (`lua -v`; its `_VERSION` string prints only `Lua 5.4`, so a run log naming one is not
evidence of the other) — the device whose path lives behind the `device-path` marker at
`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:24-29` — and every construct this project bans parses **and runs** there. Probed
in one pass 2026-09-28 through the interpreter's stdin (no file written): `7//2` printed `3`, a `goto skip` over
dead code landed on its `::skip::` label, `5&3 5|3 5~1 1<<3` printed `1 7 4 8`, `utf8.len("ab")` printed `2`, and
a `\z`-escaped literal parsed. Two further divergences do not even fail loudly: `-7 % 3` printed `2` and
`math.floor(-2.5)` printed `-3` — where the 5.1-family reader gives `-1` and a truncating rule wants `-2`, as
recorded at `docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:405-416`. So a passing local run is evidence about *values*, never a
subset certificate — a green run on a payload that used `//` would be a false all-clear of exactly the shape
`AGENTS.md` § *Stack & platform* warns about.
**The device dialect is unknown, and the two doc editions disagree about it.** The mirrored corpus states
"the runtime uses Lua 5.3" (`docs/official-docs-mirror-en-us/knowledge/appendix/mhtakr07vej4.md:61`, raw feed
`:486`; CN twin `docs/official-docs-mirror-zh-cn/knowledge/appendix/mhtakr07vej4.md:29`), unconfirmed in-editor,
and both lines sit under a repo-authored heading — our transcription, not miHoYo's words. The standard-library
blacklists **contradict each other across editions** (EN `mhtakr07vej4.md:63-72`): the EN list makes all of
`math` unavailable except `math.modf`, `math.ult`, `math.isnan`, `math.isinf` and does not list `coroutine`;
the CN list makes `coroutine.*` unavailable and does not blacklist `math` at all, presenting `math.isnan` and
`math.isinf` as *additions*. One of the two readings must be wrong about the device, and nothing here decides
which. The dialect probe stays open in `issue-tracker/open/` (the `<lua-dialect-probe>` pointer at
`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:29`).
A Lua-5.x VM written in JS is already vendored at `dev/beyond-simulator/node_modules/fengari/` (its `src/`,
`README.md`, `test/` on disk; the tracked-node-modules defect that put it there is
`issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-013-open-tracked-node-modules-in-dev-simulator.md`).
## Decision
1. **What "platform-free core" means.** A module under `platform-free-core/` is plain Lua over plain
serialisable data. It names **no** platform call (`game.*`, the `script` global, `Enum`), no client control,
no save variable's runtime form, no coordinate, no cap or budget figure, no clock; it calls no `io`, `os` or
`debug`; it uses no global (one module table per file); `require` resolves only to core siblings; and it
stores no platform handle of either id kind (`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:379-390`). The directory's own
module laws — RNG in/decision out, no input mutation, queries answer rather than raise, locale keys not
strings, the flush-then-bail `self_check()` — stand as written in `platform-free-core/README.md`
§ *Law the modules follow*.
2. **Organisation is not withheld.** The core may be laid out per surface and per shared concern. What
`AGENTS.md` opens as a question is *layout* — screens, controls, scene and asset trees (see
`docs/specs/platform-facts.md` § *Open questions*) — and a pure-rule
module claims none of it (`platform-free-core/README.md` § *The no-source-layout law*). This is the
`<organisation ADR id>` of `CONTEXT.md:38`.
3. **The interpreter is a development tool, never a project dependency.** It ships nothing and no artifact
requires it (`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:24-29`).
4. **A static gate module enforces the subset.** Because the runtime cannot (Context above), the 5.1-safe
subset is policed by a gate that *reads source text*, not by a green run: a tool that scans every
`platform-free-core/**/*.lua` file outside `dev/` for the banned constructs, for `io`/`os` use in a module,
and for the two silent-divergence traps, run under the same carve-out, its red line recorded and never
hidden. It is **required and not yet on disk** — measured: this directory held `README.md`,
`example_module.lua`, `dev/run_tests.lua` at `7e52c97` — and it is the deliverable of
`issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-026-open-lua-subset-and-io-linter-tool.md` (file wall `dev/lua-gate/**`), the
ticket this record answers for the findings recorded in `ISSUE-014` (the 5.4.5 run), `ISSUE-015` (the
`io`/`os` ban unenforced locally) and `ISSUE-016` (the stdlib blacklist contradicting the shipped example
maps). Its hand-checked per-module table stays the `NOTES.md`-style design record
`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:417-422` already demands; the gate automates that record, it does not
replace the reading.
5. **Dev-tool directories are sanctioned tracked tools, and the permission is one-way.** The carve-out covers
`platform-free-core/dev/` and any development tool this project's own tickets place beside it — the runner
`dev/run_tests.lua` may do what a tool does (file reads, a non-zero exit; its guarded `os.exit` at
`platform-free-core/dev/run_tests.lua:53`), and so does the gate of clause 4 wherever its ticket's file wall
puts it (`dev/lua-gate/**`, per `ISSUE-026`). **No shipping payload module and no platform-free-core module
`require`s anything under a `dev/` tree**, and no payload file reads or writes a file (`AGENTS.md`
§ *Stack & platform*); nothing under `dev/` is a dependency shelf, and the vendored `node_modules` already
sitting in `dev/beyond-simulator/` stays the tracked-tooling defect `ISSUE-013` records rather than becoming
a precedent for shipping a dependency. Measured 2026-09-28: the runner as it stands writes no file, resolves
its modules through `package.path` and prints `checks=8 failures=0 / PASS` for the shipped example.
6. **Write to the strictest reading of the disputed stdlib.** Where the editions contradict each other, the
core provides its own portable Lua for `floor`, `ceil`, `sqrt`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `mod`, `random` (seeded,
in/out per `docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:423-429`) and `shuffle`, and treats `math.*` as *possibly absent*
rather than as a dependency to wait for (`AGENTS.md` § *Stack & platform*, "The runtime hands you nothing").
7. **`fengari` is an optional later cross-check, not a dependency.** Nothing in `platform-free-core/` may
require it, and no build or test pipeline is built on it; a second reader's verdict may be recorded as dated
evidence when someone chooses to run one.
## Consequences
- This record is the value for `AGENTS.md:73` and `:133`'s `<platform-free-core ADR id>`, for both ids in
`CONTEXT.md:36-42` (its § *Platform-free core* term row) — the integrator lands those edits; this wave's file
wall does not include them. The `<carve-out ADR id>` slot in `platform-free-core/README.md`
§ *The carve-out law* is filled inside this same change.
- The core's merge gate now has two halves: `checks=N failures=0` from the runner **and** a green line from the
static gate. Until the gate exists, the hand-checked subset table alone carries the burden, and a module
landing without either is a defect.
- Portable `math` shims are core work, not a shortcut: the shuffle, the seeded generator and the arithmetic
helpers are this project's code by design.
- Open, and named: the device dialect (the `issue-tracker/open/` dialect probe, whose in-editor half no agent
may close), the real per-file script-size cap and what it does to the comment-shadowing ruling
(`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:373-378`), and every A1–A9 row — this record closes none of them, and no
clause above implies a confirmed platform figure.

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, named under Stack below; do not copy a row here. A rule that is still true about how to work is a `law-` file under `docs/guides/`; a product or content rule is an ADR under `docs/adr/`. The template keeps a durable-rule shelf of its own, inside that checkout and not this repository. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. A `build` or `scratchpad` folder is disposable and never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5. Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-014-open-local-lua-54-runs-forbidden-constructs.md`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, which is outside this repository: `C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `AAAAA` device, `C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` on the `TZ` device. This repo's `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` is only a pointer to it. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.
<!-- device-path: C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template ; C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template -->

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7. Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. One exception: measured platform rows live in the template checkout, not in this repo, which is why Stack names them by absolute path. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block, as Stack's does. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.
